changelog.1.0: Phase 5 (R3-CHAIN Final Research-Alignment Implementation Specification): copies config/demo_assumptions_joint_study_v2.json verbatim and adds one new top-level `research_experiment` section (RA-GOV/DATA/LOAD/SENS). Three representative steady-state load states (never transient/hourly), a small deterministic sensitivity study, and a decision_policy naming the new annualized_system_lcoh_eur_per_mwh objective (primary_objective_ranking, reusing config/joint_study_synthetic_v2.json's own indicative_system_lcoh_eur_per_mwh materiality thresholds -- same unit, same order of magnitude). load_states[].annual_duration_hours sum to exactly 5000.0, matching config/demo_assumptions.json's own economics.annual_full_load_hours.value (the base_assumptions this layer's annualized economics actually uses) -- NOT this file's own top-level economics.annual_full_load_hours=5000.0, which is a separate, canonical-shape value only consumed for this run type's own WorkflowAuditRecord, exactly as run_joint_workflow_v2() already does for the v2 run type.

_meta.description: Provisional configuration for the R3-CHAIN research-experiment layer. Every research_experiment.* value is a labelled synthetic_assumption demonstration fixture, NOT a claimed engineering standard or a validated load profile. Every other section is unchanged from config/demo_assumptions_joint_study_v2.json.
_meta.pressure_convention: All pressure fields in this project are ABSOLUTE pressures in bar (suffix _bar_abs) — this is a project-level reporting convention, not what pandapipes itself computes. VERIFIED (T2.2A, tests/network/test_pressure_semantics.py) against installed pandapipes 0.14.0: pandapipes' res_junction.p_bar is GAUGE pressure (relative to atmosphere), not absolute. Every _bar_abs config value is converted to gauge via network/pressure.py::to_gauge_bar() immediately before any pandapipes create_* call, and every res_junction.p_bar is converted back to absolute via to_absolute_bar() immediately before comparison against a _bar_abs gate or KPI reporting. Raw pandapipes gauge output must never be compared directly against a _bar_abs value anywhere in this project.

questions_without_config_impact.Q9: MCP server topology - governs architecture, recorded in ADR-001 D6/D7, no numeric config value.
questions_without_config_impact.Q10: Hosting and PyDoublet licence - governs distribution, recorded in ADR-001 D7, no numeric config value.

coupling_assumptions.minimum_auxiliary_circulation_fraction_n: Unchanged from config/demo_assumptions_joint_study_v2.json -- see network/candidate.py's own module docstring for why a load state with much-reduced demand is a genuine, evidenced risk area for this exact margin (Phase-0 audit finding, workflow/load_state_evaluation.py's own module docstring).

producer_wellhead_temperature.agreement_tolerance_basis: floating_point_safety_margin_not_a_physical_claim; primary and legacy fields are bit-identical by construction in every observed fixture. Checked via math.isclose(primary, legacy, rel_tol=agreement_relative_tolerance_fraction, abs_tol=agreement_absolute_tolerance_c) — the absolute tolerance is the binding term at this magnitude, the relative tolerance is supplementary.
producer_wellhead_temperature.note: See ADR-002 for the full source evidence and policy. No longer an unsupported array-index assumption; Dr. Jan's domain-owner confirmation is still pending.

scenario_identity._note: scenario_identifier identifies the SCENARIO (stable across repeated executions of the same PyDoublet configuration); result_identifier identifies THIS SPECIFIC raw result instance via its canonical content hash. Never conflate the two.
scenario_identity.scenario_identifier_fallback_policy: when the scenario-name field is absent, scenario_identifier is derived from a caller-supplied SourceProvenance.scenario_identifier — a real scenario identifier the caller explicitly asserts. It is never derived from source_pydoublet_commit, source_format_hint, or a raw-result content hash — none of those are scenario identifiers.

calculation_mode_policy._note: T1.5 supports only deterministic PyDoublet coupling results. SourceProvenance.calculation_mode must be explicitly 'deterministic' for parsing to proceed at all.

legacy_run_count_correction._note: Corrects the known PyDoublet legacy defect where actual_runs_completed was copy-pasted from monte_carlo_runs despite exactly one deterministic run executing.
legacy_run_count_correction.ambiguous_case_policy: if the reported actual_runs_completed does not exactly match monte_carlo_runs under trusted legacy provenance, calculation mode is treated as uncertain and validation fails rather than guessing the true run count.

candidates._note: Unchanged from config/demo_assumptions_joint_study_v2.json (legacy v1 shape, unused by the v2/research-experiment layer's own site-linked routes).

annual_full_load_hours.note: Unchanged from config/demo_assumptions_joint_study_v2.json -- see this file's own _meta.changelog note on why this value is NOT what governs research_experiment.load_states' own durations.

research_experiment._note: Phase 5, R3-CHAIN Final Research-Alignment Implementation Specification. Every value below is a labelled, illustrative synthetic demonstration fixture (spec §1.7.1's own sanctioned path for values not yet separately approved) -- never a validated load profile, cost sensitivity range, or engineering threshold.
research_experiment.referenced_study_package_expected_sha256: SHA-256 of config/joint_study_synthetic_v2.json's raw file bytes at the time this config was written. Declared and structurally validated (data_contracts.research_experiment.ResearchExperimentConfig) but NOT byte-verified against the actual loaded package content in this phase -- a stated limitation, matching economics/joint_costing.py's own identical, already-documented limitation for base_assumptions_sha256.

load_states.label: Peak demand (100% of design consumer demand)
Shoulder demand (65% of design consumer demand)
Base demand (35% of design consumer demand)

research_experiment.load_states_note: Three REPRESENTATIVE STEADY-STATE conditions (spec's own explicit scope boundary), never a transient/hourly time series. Durations sum to exactly annualization.horizon_hours_per_year (5000.0 h/a) -- enforced structurally by ResearchExperimentConfig's own validator, not merely documented here. The 'base' state (35% demand, largest deliverable-geothermal-heat-over-demand surplus ratio of the three) is the one most likely to exercise network/candidate.py's own documented curtailment-margin risk area (Phase-0 audit finding) -- reported honestly per load state if it occurs, never masked. All three states are implicitly mandatory (v1.0 schema note, data_contracts/research_experiment.py::LoadStateDefinition): the specification's own optional required_for_feasibility field is not implemented since every state declared here must be mandatory for this experiment's own scientific question -- reserved for a future schema version.
research_experiment.annualization_note: The specification's own illustrative AnnualizationPolicy example uses horizon_hours_per_year=8760.0 (a full calendar year). This experiment declares 5000.0 instead -- NOT a full calendar year, but this experiment's own REPRESENTED geothermal/DH operating-hours horizon, matching config/demo_assumptions.json's own economics.annual_full_load_hours.value (the base_assumptions this layer's annualized economics actually consumes via economics/joint_costing.py::load_base_assumptions(), referenced through joint_study_v2 -> config/joint_study_synthetic_v2.json's own economics.base_assumptions_package_relative_path). The three load_states above are not intended to tile a full 8760-hour calendar year -- only this smaller, explicitly declared operating regime -- so 5000.0 is the correct horizon for THIS experiment, not a deviation from it. The five boolean/enum fields inside annualization are not configurable toggles: they are a checked, honest restatement of what economics/annualized_system_costing.py::compute_annualized_system_economics() always does (every OPEX term included, CAPEX annualized once, useful heat is consumer-delivered heat) -- ResearchExperimentConfig's own validator rejects any other combination.

objective.name: indicative_geothermal_lcoh_at_hx_eur_per_mwh
objective.rationale: source-side LCOH at the HX boundary only (no connection/network cost) -- ranks resource SCENARIOS individually, never collapsed per site (spec's own explicit rule). Materiality thresholds reused unchanged from decision_policy.objectives[0] below, since both are the same unit and the same order of magnitude.

research_experiment.baselines_note: network_only.reference_site_id/reference_resource_scenario_id is an EXPLICIT, provenance-visible declaration (spec §11.2: 'the policy must name one existing validated synthetic resource scenario and its site') -- workflow/research_experiment.py validates that this scenario genuinely exists and belongs to this site in the referenced v2 package before any load-state evaluation runs. site_alpha/scenario_alpha_golden is the SAME pair a prior lexicographic-auto-selection implementation would have picked (sorted by (surface_site_id, resource_scenario_id), site_alpha/scenario_alpha_golden sorts first among config/joint_study_synthetic_v2.json's own 4 scenarios) -- this declaration makes that choice explicit and auditable rather than changing it. geothermal_only.resource_scenario_ids=null means every scenario in the referenced package is ranked individually (config/joint_study_synthetic_v2.json has two scenarios on one site -- scenario_alpha_golden and scenario_alpha_reduced_flow, both site_alpha -- both are ranked as separate entries, never collapsed to one best-site value). network_only.eligible_attachment_ids=null means every attachment eligible under the declared reference scenario is ranked (decision/research_comparison.py::rank_network_only_baseline() now genuinely applies this filter to the network-only subset when a non-null list is declared -- a prior implementation declared this field but never referenced it in code, a documentation-only defect corrected in the third conformance round); this filter never restricts the INTEGRATED baseline's own search universe.

sensitivity_cases.label: +20% connection-pipe CAPEX
sensitivity_cases.reason: illustrative deterministic what-if on connection-pipe construction cost -- never a probabilistic P10/P50/P90 estimate

sensitivity_cases.label: 10% geothermal deliverable-heat derating
sensitivity_cases.reason: illustrative deterministic what-if on geothermal resource availability (e.g. reservoir underperformance) -- never a probabilistic estimate, never a geological exploration-risk model, and never a new PyDoublet simulation. This case re-derives ECONOMICS only from already-computed KPIs (auxiliary heat rises to cover exactly the derated shortfall; total_heat_delivered_kw and mass/energy balance are unchanged for every load state); it never re-runs pandapipes or the HX evaluator, so it structurally cannot discover a new technical infeasibility. dh_hydraulic_pumping_power_kw is held at its base-case value as a documented simplification (see decision/research_comparison.py::_apply_sensitivity_case()) rather than re-derived for the slightly smaller actual injected mass flow.

objectives.name: annualized_system_lcoh_eur_per_mwh
objectives.rationale: primary annualized system cost signal across representative load states -- materiality thresholds reused unchanged from config/joint_study_synthetic_v2.json's own indicative_system_lcoh_eur_per_mwh objective, since both are the same unit and the same order of magnitude
